## Learning goals

- I can identify the main hardware and operating-system details of a Linux computer.
- I can compare what the desktop shows with command-line evidence.
- I can state clearly when a sensor or value is not available.

## Inspect the computer

Start with **Settings > System Info** or the closest system-information page on your desktop. Record the computer name, Linux version, processor, memory, and storage.

Then open Terminal and try:

```bash
hostnamectl
lscpu
free -h
lsblk
df -h
uptime
```

Match each command to the information you found in the desktop. `lsblk` lists storage devices. `df -h` shows used and available file-system space.

## Watch the computer work

Run `htop` or `top`. Open another program, then watch CPU and memory use change. Don't treat one instant reading as a full performance test.

If the teacher has installed `lm-sensors`, run `sensors`. Sensor support varies by computer. Record the sensor's label and units. If a temperature or power value isn't available, write **not available** instead of guessing.

## Activity

Create a one-page inventory with:

- computer name and model if known
- Linux version
- CPU model and core count
- installed and available memory
- storage device and free space
- one screenshot of `htop`
- one difference between the desktop information and the command output

## Check your work

Every value should name its source. A screenshot without a short explanation is not enough.
